title: Dual-seed time split with independent chains
spec: Split the time budget into three independent chains: each runs fresh starts for 25% of the budget then basin hops from its own best for 10%. At the end return the best of the three. Differs from the elite pool because chains never share state, which preserves diversity across basins.

title: Boundary-biased circle count perturbation
spec: In basin hopping, with probability 0.5 apply jitter only to circles whose centre lies within 0.25 of the square boundary using sd 0.05, and leave interior circles unmoved; otherwise use the existing jitter. Best packings typically have a rigid interior and flexible boundary arrangement.

title: Compression-based starts (Lubachevsky-like)
spec: For half of fresh starts, generate initial centres by simulating a quick event-free compression: start 32 random points, run 150 steps where each point is pushed away from neighbours with force 1/d^3 (clip step 0.01) and pushed inside the box, with a growing virtual radius used to scale the force range. Then use these centres with the common-radius SLSQP stage. Distinct from the earlier 1/d^2 repulsion test by using growth-scaled range and many more steps.

title: Radius-ordered structured start
spec: For fresh starts, draw per-circle target radii from a bimodal distribution (about 12 big circles of 0.11 and 20 small circles of 0.06), place centres by sequential random dart throwing largest first so no target discs overlap (reduce radii by 0.9 each 200 failed attempts), then run the common-radius stage and the main SLSQP with these radii as the initial radii. Known good packings of this problem have mixed sizes.

title: Larger MAX_ITER with basin-hopping only
spec: Set MAX_ITER to 400 only for the basin-hopping phase calls (start is not None), leaving fresh starts at 200, so late refinements converge fully.

title: Remove-and-reinsert into largest hole
spec: In the basin-hopping phase, with probability 0.5 build the perturbed start by taking the best packing, removing the smallest 1-3 circles, and placing each at the point (from 2000 random candidates in the square) maximising the minimum of distance to other circles' surfaces (distance to centre minus radius) and wall distance, giving it a radius equal to that clearance (min 0.01). Then run the normal SLSQP polish from this start (with the neighbour-pruned constraints) and accept if the repaired sum improves. Otherwise use the existing Gaussian jitter.

title: Time-sliced schedule with a final tight-ftol refinement
spec: Reserve the last 10% of the time budget. Spend it running SLSQP with ftol=1e-12 and maxiter 500 on the best packing and on its top two distinct alternatives from earlier. Apply _repair to each result and keep the best. Spend the first 90% as it is now, with TIME_FRACTION 0.8 replaced by the equivalent split. SLSQP's default ftol of 1e-6 may stop short of full convergence.

title: Batch of cheap starts, top-k refinement
spec: Generate 12 fresh starts at a time through the common-radius stage only (cheap), compute a quick score for each as the sum of radii after a 30-iteration main SLSQP, then fully refine only the best 2 with the full MAX_ITER. Repeat this batch cycle until 40% of the time is used, then proceed to basin hopping as before.

title: Hex-lattice initialisation
spec: Start from a hex-like lattice with row counts such as 6,5,6,5,6,4 (adjusted to 32), with random jitter and a random rotation of the row structure. Use the radii of about 0.08.

title: Cache constraint index arrays and use float32-free vectorised neighbour list
spec: Precompute triu indices once per n in a module-level dict, and in the main SLSQP use an analytic Jacobian only for the pair block via scipy sparse-to-dense assembly, built with np.zeros and fancy indexing. Ignore wall rows in the Jacobian by providing bounds instead of wall constraints. Goal is purely speed: more restarts in 24 s.

title: Batch of perturbations screened with short SLSQP
spec: In the basin-hopping phase, generate 6 jittered copies of the best packing at once. Run SLSQP with maxiter 30 on each. Continue only the one with the best repaired sum of radii to maxiter 200. This gives a cheap best-of-k selection per step, so most of the compute goes to promising moves.

title: Use trust-constr-free SLSQP with warm-started multipliers by two-round solve
spec: Run the main SLSQP twice per fresh start: first with maxiter 80, then restart from the result with a 0.005 centre jitter limited to circles whose radius is below the median, maxiter 120. Keep the better of the two. The second round lets small circles escape bad pockets without a full basin hop.

title: Contact-graph guided perturbation: free the loosest circles
spec: In basin hopping, compute for each circle of the best packing how many contacts it has (gap < 1e-6, walls included). Choose circles with 2 or fewer contacts, the rattlers, and re-place them at random inside the largest empty region. Pick the region by evaluating 500 random points and taking the one with the largest distance to the nearest circle edge. Then run SLSQP. Circles with few contacts are wasted area.

title: Sorted-radii structured start
spec: For half of fresh starts, draw initial radii from a bimodal distribution (about 12 large circles of 0.11 and 20 small of 0.07). Place centres by sequential largest-first random rejection sampling so that no circles overlap. Then run the common-radius stage and the main SLSQP from those radii and positions. This seeds the large/small mix that the best known packings have.

title: Sorted-radii structured start
spec: For half of fresh starts after the common-radius stage, set per-circle initial radii to a bimodal pattern: 20 circles at 0.10 and 12 at 0.07 (randomly assigned), scaled so the sum equals the common-radius result times 32. Centres come from the common-radius solution. This mimics the large and small mix found in best known packings.

title: Radius-spread starting radii from sorted sizes
spec: After the common-radius stage, set initial per-circle radii by a structured two-size pattern: the circles with the 8 largest distances to their nearest neighbours get radius 1.4*r_common and the rest get 0.9*r_common (clipped to wall distance). Use these as x0 radii for the main SLSQP. Optimal packings for this problem have mixed sizes, so this seeds the size heterogeneity.

title: Basin hopping from the best of two independent halves
spec: Run fresh restarts in two independent pools, each for 20% of the time, using separate rng streams. Take the better pool's best, then run basin hopping for the rest of the time. Also give the second pool's best a 20% chance of being the basin-hopping start, to diversify.

title: Use trust-constr alternative
spec: For the polishing of the best 3 candidates, run scipy trust-constr with analytic gradients, then repair. Check that it escapes the SLSQP stalls.

title: Final LP-plus-tight SLSQP polish of top candidates in the last second
spec: Reserve the final 8% of the time (TIME_FRACTION stays 0.8 but additionally use leftover 0.1*time_limit): run SLSQP with ftol=1e-13 and maxiter 1000 on the best packing with only near-neighbour (d<0.05) constraints, then repair, and keep it if the sum improves. Avoid anything but one extra call.

title: Wall bounds instead of wall constraints
spec: In the main SLSQP, drop the four wall inequality blocks and the r>=0 block from cons. Pass bounds to minimize: centres in [0,1], radii in [0,0.5]. Add linear wall constraints only for c-r>=0 and 1-c-r>=0 if needed to stay valid. The aim is a smaller constraint vector (fewer rows, faster QP steps), and so more restarts in the same time. Keep _repair as it is.

title: Remove one circle, solve 31, re-add with LP
spec: In the late phase, take the best packing and delete a random circle. Re-optimise the remaining 31 with SLSQP (maxiter 100). Then insert a new circle at the largest empty spot, found by sampling 5000 points and picking the one with the biggest distance-to-nearest-circle-surface. Run the full SLSQP on all 32 from there. Accept as best if it improves.

title: Batch of perturbed copies, keep best by short run
spec: In basin hopping, generate 8 perturbed copies of the best packing (sd uniform in 0.01 to 0.04), run each through SLSQP with maxiter 30, then continue the top 2 to maxiter 200. Different from earlier screening because it screens on the perturbation scale and runs two finalists to convergence.

title: Increase MAX_ITER to 500
spec: Set MAX_ITER=500 so that SLSQP converges fully in each run instead of stopping at 200 iterations. Best combined with an analytic Jacobian.

title: Size-structured start with big/small mix
spec: For fresh starts, draw target radii from a bimodal mix, with 8 circles near 0.13 and 24 near 0.08. Place centres by Poisson-disc dart throwing, largest first, using those radii. Set the initial radii variables to 0.8 times the targets and skip the common-radius stage. The best known packings have mixed radii, so this starts closer to them. Slot 43 used something similar, so make this one deterministic about the counts and add no jitter beyond the placement.

title: Randomised radius-weighted objective
spec: For a fresh start, run the first SLSQP stage (maxiter 60) with the objective -sum(w_i r_i), where w_i is uniform in [0.7, 1.3] per circle, drawn from rng. This tilts the landscape toward different size distributions. Then run the true -sum(r) objective from that point with maxiter 200. It diversifies the basins reached.

title: Exact LP radius re-optimisation after each SLSQP
spec: After each _solve_once, with the centres fixed, solve the radius LP with scipy.optimize.linprog (maximise sum r s.t. r_i+r_j<=d_ij, r_i<=wall distances, r>=0, method highs), then apply a tiny shrink of 1e-10 and verify validity. Use the LP radii for comparing candidates and for selecting the best. Compare candidates by this value so that basin-hopping chooses on true quality.

title: Two-pool tournament with successive halving
spec: Run 8 fresh starts, each with SLSQP at maxiter 60, then keep the top 3 and continue them to maxiter 200. Repeat this cycle until 40% of the time is used. Then run the existing basin hopping from the best packing. This allocates the budget by successive halving.

title: Soft-min size-spread regulariser decaying to zero
spec: For fresh starts, run the main SLSQP in three stages with objective -sum(r) + lam*sum((r-mean(r))**2) and lam = 0.5, 0.15, 0 at maxiter 40, 40 and 120. The early spread penalty favours uniform sizes, which keeps the optimizer away from degenerate tiny-circle local optima. The final stage uses the true objective.

title: Log-barrier interior-point start
spec: For fresh starts, replace the common-radius SLSQP stage by 30 gradient steps. Each step is on the sum of -log(gap) barrier terms, with analytic gradients for pairs and walls, with a common radius of 0.06 and a step size that keeps all gaps positive. Then run the main SLSQP. This gives a feasible, well-spread start.

title: Wall bounds instead of wall constraints
spec: Pass bounds to SLSQP: centres in [0,1] and radii in [0,0.5]. Remove the wall-gap and r>=0 blocks from the main constraint function, but keep the 4n wall constraints for the centre-to-wall distance, because bounds alone do not enforce c-r>=0. Also precompute and cache the pair index arrays. The aim is a faster, cheaper SLSQP iteration.

title: Bounds for wall constraints
spec: Remove the 4n wall constraints and the r>=0 constraints in the main SLSQP, and pass bounds instead: centres in [0,1], radii in [0,0.5]. Instead enforce the walls by reparametrising: keep wall inequality constraints only for circles but not... Simpler: keep the wall constraints but add bounds to the variables (centres [0,1], radii [0,0.5]) to reduce wasted steps, and drop the separate r constraint rows. Verify the final repair still ensures validity.

title: Lower SLSQP ftol in main solve with more iterations in fresh starts
spec: Pass options ftol=1e-10 and maxiter=300 to the main SLSQP, and cut fresh starts that have not reached sum of radii above 2.85 after the first 60 iterations. To do this, run in two calls: maxiter 60, check the sum of radii, then continue from the result only if it is promising. Spend the saved time on extra restarts.

title: Smaller common-radius init
spec: In the cheap common-radius SLSQP stage for fresh starts, set the initial common radius to 0.03 instead of INIT_RADIUS 0.05. Keep everything else the same. This tests how sensitive the starting basin is to the initial radius.

title: Fewer pair constraints via cell list in main solve
spec: For fresh starts, after the common-radius stage keep only pairs whose centre distance is below 0.35 in the main SLSQP, and re-check all pairs afterwards. If any pair is violated, rerun with the full set from the result. This reduces SLSQP cost per iteration (496 pairs to roughly 150), giving more restarts within the time limit.

title: Batch of 4 jittered starts for the best-of selection
spec: In each fresh-start iteration, build 4 random initial points, run only the cheap common-radius SLSQP stage on each, and run the full main SLSQP only on the one with the largest common radius. This is a cheap pre-selection of starts by quality, not by the loss of a full run.

title: Cosine time-varying jitter with periodic restarts
spec: After 40% of the time, run basin hopping in cycles of 8 iterations. Within each cycle, the jitter sd decays from 0.04 to 0.005. At the start of each cycle reset the base packing to the global best. This is a sawtooth schedule that alternates exploration and exploitation.

title: Ring-boundary structured starts
spec: For half of fresh starts, place about 12 circle centres along the square's boundary at distance 0.08 from the walls, evenly spaced with jitter, and the rest uniformly random in the interior [0.2,0.8]^2. Best known packings tend to have a ring of boundary circles around an irregular interior. Then run the usual common-radius SLSQP and main SLSQP.

title: Higher MAX_ITER in basin-hopping only
spec: Keep MAX_ITER=200 for fresh starts but pass maxiter=500 and ftol=1e-10 to SLSQP when start is not None (the basin-hopping phase), so that perturbed local refinements converge fully to tight local optima. Implement by adding a maxiter parameter to _solve_once.

title: Swap big/small circle radii move
spec: In the basin-hopping phase, with probability 0.5 pick one of the 8 largest and one of the 8 smallest circles of the best packing, swap their centre positions (radii stay attached to the circles' original slots, so the big circle lands in the small one's place), add jitter sd 0.01, then run SLSQP. Otherwise do the existing Gaussian perturbation. Accept if the repaired sum improves.

title: Swap-neighbour radii exchange in basin hopping
spec: In basin hopping, with probability 0.4 pick two touching circles with different radii (centre distance within 1e-4 of r_i+r_j) and exchange their centre positions, scaling nothing else. Then run SLSQP from there with the usual jitter of sd 0.005. This is a local permutation move that keeps the contact network almost valid.

title: Radius-sorted rank-preserving perturbation
spec: In basin hopping, instead of jittering centres, perturb the radii: multiply each radius by exp(N(0,0.15)) and then shrink all radii by a common factor to remove overlaps. Keep the centres of the best packing and run SLSQP from there. This explores the size distribution while keeping the layout.

title: Adaptive time split by improvement rate
spec: Replace the fixed 0.4 switch with an adaptive rule. Keep a running log of fresh-start results. Switch to basin hopping when the best fresh result was found more than 30% of the elapsed time ago, or at 0.55 of the time limit at the latest. In the basin-hopping phase, return to fresh starts for one run after 8 consecutive failures to improve. Do not use a stagnation count of restarts alone (slot 33 did that). This version uses elapsed-time-since-best.

title: Event-driven billiards compression start
spec: For half of fresh starts, make initial centres with a simple Lubachevsky-Stillinger-style procedure. Give 32 random points random velocities. Grow the common radius from 0.02 in steps of 0.002 and resolve overlaps by pushing apart overlapping pairs along their line of centres, for 200 vectorised numpy sweeps with wall clamping. Then run the main SLSQP from those centres with radii set to the achieved radius. Use the achieved radius instead of the common-radius SLSQP stage.

title: Power-mean objective continuation
spec: In the main SLSQP for fresh starts, optimise the objective -(mean(r^p))^(1/p)*n, with p=0.5 for the first 60 iterations (it favours equal-sized circles), then p=1 (the true sum) for the remaining iterations, warm-started from the previous result. The aim is to reach different basins than a direct sum objective. Use only the true sum for comparing candidates.

title: Smaller-circle count continuation
spec: For fresh starts, first solve a 28-circle problem with the cheap common-radius SLSQP and then the main SLSQP with maxiter 60. Then add 4 circles at the centres of the largest empty holes. Find the holes by sampling 2000 random points and taking the points with the largest clearance, spreading them out. Give the new circles radius 0.02 and run the full main SLSQP on all 32. This builds on a structured, relaxed packing.

title: Reduced-variable SLSQP with fixed small circles
spec: In the late phase, perturb the best packing, then run SLSQP on only the variables of a random local cluster (a random circle plus its 8 nearest neighbours). The other circles are frozen, and constraints between the cluster and frozen circles are kept. This has about 27 variables, so each solve is far cheaper, which allows many more local moves. Then run one full SLSQP with maxiter 60 when the local result improves the sum.

title: Batch-evaluated vectorised penalty relaxation
spec: Write a numpy function that runs 64 random starts at once as an (B,n,2) array. It does 200 steps of gradient descent with momentum on a penalty energy: overlap^2 plus wall violation^2, minus the radius sum, with the radii as variables. Take the best 3 by penalised score and polish them with the existing SLSQP. Use this for the first 15% of the time to seed the best packing.

title: Cheaper SLSQP via active pair pruning in basin hopping
spec: In basin hopping, build the pair list from the perturbed centres with a cutoff on gap < 0.08 instead of 0.15. Then run SLSQP. After the run, check for violated pruned pairs. If any exist, add them and re-run for 30 iterations. This should give more basin-hopping steps per second.

title: Soft-min spread regulariser decaying to zero
spec: In fresh starts, run the main SLSQP in 3 stages with objective -sum(r) + lam*sum((r-mean(r))^2), with lam = 0.5, 0.15, 0, each stage warm-started from the previous one with maxiter about 70. The final stage must be the true objective. Use this for half of fresh starts.

title: Radius-inflation continuation
spec: For fresh starts, run SLSQP on the sum of r^p with p=0.5 for 40 iterations (it favours equal radii), then p=1. The total iteration count stays the same as now. The common-radius init stays as the first stage.

title: Two-size-class constrained basin hop
spec: In the late phase, take the best packing and sort the radii. Perturb by adding noise to the radii of the 6 smallest circles (sd 0.02) and moving their centres to random points in the largest empty space. Pick the space by sampling 300 points and taking the one furthest from every circle edge. Then run SLSQP at maxiter 200. This differs from the earlier reinsert moves because the radii get a fresh start and the 6 circles move together.

title: Shrink-and-regrow perturbation
spec: In basin hopping, start SLSQP from the best packing with all radii multiplied by 0.7 and centres jittered by sd 0.015, so the packing is loose. SLSQP can then rearrange the contact network more freely than from a jammed state. Use it for half the basin-hopping calls.
